lines.text: Pay is up 3.0%. Prices are up 3.4%.
lines.say: Pay's up three percent. Prices? Three point four.

lines.text: Pay is from Friday's jobs report, prices from August inflation. And hiring? Just 29,000 jobs in September.
lines.say: Pay is from Friday's jobs report, prices from August inflation. And hiring? Just twenty-nine thousand jobs in September.

scene.headline: US adds just 29,000 jobs in Sept

lines.text: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected 84,000.
lines.say: Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected eighty-four thousand.

lines.text: Unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, from 4.1% in August.
lines.say: Unemployment ticked up to four point two percent, from four point one in August.

lines.text: Earlier months got worse too. July now shows 10,000 jobs lost, and August was cut to 133,000.
lines.say: Earlier months got worse too. July now shows ten thousand jobs lost, and August was cut to one hundred thirty-three thousand.

lines.text: Yearly pay growth slowed to 3.0%, the lowest since May 2021. August inflation was 3.4%.
lines.say: Yearly pay growth slowed to three percent, the lowest since May twenty twenty-one, while August inflation was three point four.

lines.text: Hypothetical: $50,000 salary. A 3% raise is $1,500. Keeping pace with 3.4% inflation takes $1,700: $200 short.
lines.say: Say you earn fifty thousand dollars. A three percent raise is fifteen hundred. Keeping pace with inflation takes seventeen hundred. That's two hundred short.

lines.text: Next to watch: September inflation, the Fed's October meeting, and the October jobs report.
lines.say: Next to watch: September inflation, the Fed's October meeting, and the October jobs report.

post.title: September jobs: pay up 3%, August prices up 3.4%
post.ig:
Average pay is up 3.0%. Prices are up 3.4%.

US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September 2026; economists expected 84,000.
Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. July was revised to -10,000 jobs and August to 133,000.
Average hourly pay is up 3.0% over 12 months, the slowest since May 2021, versus 3.4% CPI inflation in August.

Sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics (Oct 2 and Sept 11, 2026); CNBC; CNN.
